_source: Generated with rmqrcode (MIT), an independent implementation of ISO/IEC 23941, via the recipe in __tests__/fixtures/README.md. Each entry is the exact module matrix it produces for that segmentation, size and level.
_segments: Every case pins its segmentation explicitly. Two encoders can both be correct and still split a string differently across modes, so comparing module matrices only means something when both are given the same segments. Our own mode selection is checked separately, by asserting it is never larger than a single-mode encoding.
_excluded: Three categories are absent, all because the reference is wrong there rather than because we are. (1) Sizes whose Reed-Solomon blocks differ in length: rmqrcode's interleaver uses break where the standard skips an exhausted block and continues, so it silently drops data codewords - one of 73 for R13x99-M, four of 76 for R17x139-H - and those symbols cannot decode. (2) R17x43-M, whose table lists a 60-codeword block against that size's own total of 61; we use 61, giving 22 error correction codewords. (3) R13x27-M, whose table lists 14 data codewords against its own stated 96 data bits, which is 12; every other entry in that table has k*8 equal to its data bits, and the two other 21-codeword sizes both split M as 12 and 9. We use 12.
